newsitem.title: USA: Ford to de-power air bags in all 1998 models.
newsitem.headline: Ford to de-power air bags in all 1998 models.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. plans to announce Thursday that it will install reduced power air bags in all of its 1998-model cars and trucks, making it the first automaker to implement new government air bag rules across its entire product range.

A Ford official said Wednesday the first vehicle to be available with the reduced-power air bags will be the 1998 Lincoln Navigator sport utility vehicle, which begins rolling off the assembly line at Ford's Wayne, Mich., truck plant on Thursday.

Earlier this year, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration issued new regulations calling for a 25 percent to 30 percent reduction in the inflation power of air bags, a move aimed at reducing the danger they pose to children and smaller adults.
The NHTSA gave automakers two years to make the change.
Air bags, which now inflate at speeds of up to 200 miles per hour, have been blamed in the deaths of 63 people in the United States, including 38 children and 25 adults.

The NHTSA also is deliberating on another proposed rule that would allow people to have their air bags disconnected. While the auto industry vigorously supported the reduction in air bag inflation power, it has adamantly opposed the proposed disconnection rule, in part due to liability concerns.
